subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been split into segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

He missed the college bus / because he woke up / unpardonably lately in the morning.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**unpardonably lately**" is incorrect because "**lately**" refers to a recent time in the past and is not suitable in the context of waking up at a specific (late) time.
 
• The correct word should be "**late**," which indicates tardiness or delay in action — suitable for time-based events like waking up late.
 
• "Unpardonably late" accurately conveys the idea of being so late that it is almost unforgivable.
 
• Therefore, the adverb "**lately**" must be replaced with the adjective "**late**" to correctly complete the phrase.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 4: unpardonably lately in the morning**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He missed the college bus because he woke up unpardonably late in the morning."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lately** means “recently” and is used for actions that happened in the near past (e.g., "I have seen him lately").
 
• **Late** refers to being delayed or not on time and is appropriate for specific moments or schedules (e.g., "He arrived late to class").
